english.title: Corruptly give / promise / offer a gift / loan / fee / advantage
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..)

(A)_[by yourself]_
(B)_[by or in conjunction with another person, namely **(..SPECIFY THE OTHER PERSON..)]_

corruptly gave, promised or offered a gift, loan, fee, reward, or advantage, namely **(..SPECIFY..), to a person, namely **(..SPECIFY THAT PERSON..), whether for the benefit of that person or of some other person, as an inducement to or reward for or otherwise on account of any member, officer, or servant of a public body, namely **(..SPECIFY THE BODY..), doing or forbearing to do something in respect of a matter or transaction, actual or proposed, in which the public body was concerned, namely **(..SPECIFY THE MATTER OR TRANSACTION..)
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 1(2) and 2 of the Public Bodies Corrupt Practices Act 1889.
english.pointstoprove:
date nd location
by yourself/by or in conjunction with another person
corruptly gave/promised/offered a gift/loan/fee/reward/advantage to a person
whether for the benefit of that person/some other person
as an inducement to/reward for/otherwise on account of
any member/officer/servant of a public body
doing/forbearing to do something in respect of a matter/transaction actual/proposed
in which the public body was concerned

investigatoraction.description: Submit a form Crimsec 38 where drugs are seized

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
This CJS Code and Standard Offence Wording document is now OBSOLETE. Repealed by the Bribery Act 2010,

(i) See also the presumption of corruption provided by section 2 of the Prevention of Corruption Act 1916.
(ii) In R v Natji (Times 14.3.02) it was decided that "Public body" (under this Act) did NOT include a government department and/or the Crown, but see the Prevention of Corruption Act 1906 which widened the definition.

other.penalty:
Summary: 6 months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: 7 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

Time limit for prosecution:
None
